resources.summary: Public sheet with 8 tabs, all fetched (htmlview, every tab as CSV, and xlsx). It is a full OLLCP list (orient all four U-layer edges and corners, and permute corners, in one alg) with no prose, no instructions and no credits. rouxcubing.com lists it under CMLL > Pinkie Pie, next to Kian's explainer video. Earlier hub research describes Pinkie Pie as using an OLLCP alg in place of CMLL to skip LSE steps 4a+4b. This sheet does not say when to use it. Structure: 7 case tabs, one per CMLL corner-orientation group (O, H, Pi, S and As together, U, L, T). Each group is split into numbered edge-orientation patterns ('OLLCP P1' to 'P8' and so on). Under each pattern, each cell holds one alg, one cell per corner-permutation subcase; most patterns have 6 subcases, O and H fewer. Some cells give a second line as an alternative. Each alg has a VisualCube plan image (cubing.net API, stage=coll) generated by an IMAGE() formula from the alg text. Algs are general 2H LL algs (many F, S, f, D, L moves) with a pre-AUF in brackets. A 'OLLCP Statistics' tab gives, for every case, its probability (1/54 for most, plus 1/1296 for a skip), STM length, expected pre-AUF and a weighted cost (overall average 10.96 STM, 11.76 weighted). It also aggregates by CO group and by OLL shape family (OCLL, ELL, Dot, C/I/L/P/T/W shapes, Fish, Knight, lightning bolts, Square, Awkward). One cell holds a cat photo with the joke text '/midoribox'. Scope caution: this is a generic last-layer set, and the shape families are CFOP OLL vocabulary. It is relevant to Roux only through Pinkie Pie.

resources.title: NMCMLL List
resources.author: Athefre (James Straughan), recognition with Gilles Roux; mapping idea credited to UNO (Fahmi Aulia Rachman)
resources.level: intermediate to advanced (includes beginner 2-look paths for people changing recognition)
resources.summary: Public sheet with 11 tabs, all fetched; the xlsx was also fetched, because the case diagrams are embedded images. NMCMLL is CMLL recognised by the L/R side colours (orange/red are assumed on L/R) instead of the U colour, so it works for both matching and non-matching blocks. The Info tab gives a 2-step method. Step 1: find how the L/R-coloured stickers are oriented, which gives the group. Step 2: check positions marked by blue lines on the group's template for 2, 1 or 0 matching colour pairs, which picks the case. Info notes that the reference positions can be moved, which allows multi-angle recognition. Info also says the method is superseded by ATCRM and links an ATCRM sheet and Athefre's ACRM page. Structure: 8 group tabs (O, H, Pi, U, T, S, AS, L). Each has numbered group rows (e.g. U1-U3) and pattern columns 1-3 or 1-4. Each cell holds the alg(s) plus a 'CMLL Name' row mapping to the standard names used in the Roux Discord 2H CMLL sheet (e.g. 'U2 - Rows'). Every case has a plan-view diagram showing only red/orange and the stickers to compare; column B holds the group template with blue comparison lines. Algs credit an external sheet (tinyurl, which redirects to a Google Sheet) plus 'other algs known and discovered over the years'. Two extra tabs hold 2-look options as single images. Option 1 orients L/R colours to the L/R sides first, then permutes (7+7 algs). Option 2 orients to U first, then permutes (7+4 algs, 'three fewer', with no solved state in the second look).

resources.title: ACMLL (ACMLL List / A3 CMLL)
resources.author: James Straughan (Athefre); sets by Aditya Pathak (L/R Flip Swap Front) and Ryan 'OreKehStrah' Hudgens (Swap FL/BR); three-sided recognition by Max Winteg
resources.summary: Public sheet with 13 visible tabs plus one hidden 'template' tab (seen only in the xlsx); all fetched. Info says the document is no longer maintained: ACMLL moved to Athefre's website (sites.google.com/site/athefre/acmll), with block types in separate sheets and better algs. Info explains ACMLL/A3 CMLL. You build F2B 'passively', leaving pairs or pieces imperfectly connected (flipped pairs, rearranged pairs, single misoriented edges or corners, pieces from the other block, unattached pairs), and CMLL fixes them. Claimed benefits: fewer moves, more planning in inspection, and good algs. It suggests inserting a pair in the orientation it was built. A movecount table compares 8 flipped-pair inserts with the normal inserts: average 2.625 vs 4.625 moves. Info lists 11 block types, each with an isometric 3D image and a setup alg: Flip, Spiral, Line, Single/Double Flipped Spiral, Swap+Flip Opposite, L/R Flip, L/R Swap Adjacent/Opposite, L/R Flip Swap Adjacent, Outside. Only some have alg tabs. Each tab is a 43-case CMLL-sized grid with a plan-view image per case. Spiral, L/R Flip Swap Front and Swap tabs use CMLL group letters O/S/AS/L/U/T/Pi/H with numbered columns. Flipped Pair tabs use groups A-H (6/6/4/6/6/6/6/3) because a twisted corner changes the U-layer orientation pattern. Flipped Pair FR adds a 'Recognition' column of yellow/magenta orientation diagrams. Info links junnoske's separate 2-look doc for some sets.

resources.title: TCMLL-N OH (franz + cordelia + tyler + alvaro's TCMLL Algs)
resources.author: franz, cordelia, tyler, alvaro (landing page credited to Yomie)
resources.summary: Public sheet with 25 tabs, all fetched as CSV and xlsx. The CSV of '1b RUF gen' alone is 5 MB. The Info tab defines TCMLL-N ('twisty Corners of the Last Layer, w/o regard to the M-slice'): one alg solves all 4 U corners plus a twisted SB last pair (tSBLP). Xa = front slot, Xb = back slot. Vanilla TCMLL (1a+2a) is 86 cases, base TCMLL-N (1x-3x) 258, and advanced (WIP, 4x-5x) 430. Info says algs are not fully optimised and invites comments. It links the OH ACMLL Discord, a CMLL visualiser, and an input doc for Tao Yu's trainer. resources.rouxers.com labels it 'algorithms only for OH'; the algs are mostly RUF / RrUM, and '*' marks algs that are not DFDB-safe. Structure: case tabs 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b, each a 43-case grid with a plan-view image per case. 1x/2x/4x/5x use groups A-H (6/6/4/6/6/6/6/3) and a 'Recognition' column of yellow/magenta orientation diagrams. 3x uses CMLL group names O/S/AS/L/U/T/Pi/H. The sheet does not define what 1-5 index; the 3x grouping fits an untwisted corner. 5b is empty and Progress says '1x-3x, 4a, 5a DONE'. Cell comments give nicknames such as 'Polarized Triangle', 'Single Bar' and 'any angle'. Tab 3a links 14 algs to YouTube Shorts execution demos. 'learning order' recommends 1a+2a, then 3ab/4ab/5ab, then 1b/2b, noting that 1-2 back-slot cases can be done with D' (alg) D but 3-5 cannot. 'TCMLL Inserts' rates which SB last-pair cases are worth inserting twisted (Amazing/Great/Good/Meh) with estimated SB moves saved (about 1 to 10) and a target of saving 2 or more moves. 'Time Attack' lays out the 86 vanilla cases as images in 8 nicknamed groups (Pac-Man, Gun, Stingray, Spaceship, Hammer, Turtle, Car, Shuriken). Nine raw batch-solver tabs hold candidate solutions scored by ESQ or MCC with STM counts, for RUF and RrUM move sets.

resources.title: TCMLL (Montu's TCMLL Algs)
resources.author: Montu (per the rouxcubing.com link text; the doc itself names nobody)
resources.summary: Public Google Doc with one tab (confirmed with Playwright); txt, docx and html-zip exports fetched. A bare alg list with no prose, instructions or credits. Two halves, 'TCMLL+' and 'TCMLL-' (the two twist directions). Each half has 8 groups named after the 2x2 TCLL shape names: Strolley (6), Gun (6), Twoface (4), Hammer (6), Spaceship (6), Turtle (6), Pinwheel (3), Pinwheel poser (6), so 43 per direction and 86 in total. Each case has one alg next to a cropped top-view screenshot (86 images in the docx). The algs use many F, L and D moves and look computer-generated rather than ergonomic. Nothing is labelled OH, so this is the 2H counterpart to the OH TCMLL sheet. The groups follow 2x2 TCLL naming, while the franz OH sheet uses letters A-H with its own nicknames.

resources.title: L5C and SL5C
resources.author: Athefre (James Straughan) (Info: 'My username everywhere is Athefre')
resources.summary: Public sheet with 8 visible tabs plus a hidden 'Raw Algs' tab (in the xlsx only: 614 cases x about 100 batch-solver candidates). All were fetched. The method context is inferred from the case images: left block + a right-side 1x2x2 (DR, BR, DBR solved), then L5C (4 U corners + DFR), then L7E (last 7 edges). Info mentions the 'right side 1x2x2' and 'L7E method' but never names the method; it looks like the 42-style Roux variant listed among advanced techniques on the hubs. SL5C algs drop the final R' or U* R' so they can cancel into L7E. Info also explains changing a final R2 to R'. Recognition (Info): if the DFR corner is on the D layer, use CLL or TCLL recognition. If it is on the U layer: (1) orientation of that D corner, (2) orientation of 3 chosen corner positions, (3) the pattern within those 3. Orientation case names are built from OCLL-name combinations (e.g. OS, OAS, LAS, SH, PH, ZZ). Tabs: CLL (DFR solved: 42 cases), TCLL+ and TCLL- (DFR twisted in place: 43 each), UO, U+ and U- (DFR on the U layer, oriented or twisted: 162 each, in 27 orientation groups x 6). Total 614 L5C cases, each with an L5C and an SL5C alg block. Two images per case use VisualCube with a custom facelet mask (iso and plan). 'Two Look' gives OL5C (23 orientation cases, average 7.96 moves, or 5.96 for SOL5C) plus PL5C; Info says 31 algs, and suggests DFR corner + OCLL + PCLL (9 algs) as an easier route to full CLL. All algs were made with the batch solver.
